column1: Slot-resolve every name at parse time, not only inside fast loops
column2: Performance assessment relayed by Ahmed 2026-09-10; agent_co follow-up in agent_co.txt
column3: PURSUE -- premise VERIFIED: env is HashMap<String, Value> (lib.rs:3301) and frames Vec<HashMap<String, Value>> (3314), so each name read outside the fast path hashes a string. Register machinery already exists to extend: FastExpr (3909), eval_fast(e, regs: &[f64]) (3921), CompiledFn (4769). Needs no JIT.

column3: OPEN, but its headline example is STALE: the "while is 29x slower" figure was fixed -- BACKLOG.md:377 marks it [x], "measured at 1.1x now". The remaining claim (any call in the body ejects the loop to the tree walker) was NOT verified. Measure before scoping.

column1: Fuse array expressions (Y = A .* B + C) into one element loop before evaluating
column3: PURSUE per agent_co. Removes one intermediate array: 6 logical element reads/writes become 4. agent_co is explicit that this does NOT establish a speedup -- caches, compile cost, SIMD and size all matter. Gate: measure correctness, elapsed, prep, repeat-call time and allocated bytes on small AND large arrays; cover NaN/inf/signed-zero and aliasing; no FP reassociation or fma contraction that changes rounding.

column1: Cache prepared execution plans and widen the existing scalar register tier
column3: PURSUE per agent_co, CONDITIONAL on profiles showing repeated preparation is material. Note it corrects a common misreading: whole-function caching already EXISTS (CompiledFn ~4769), so this is extension, not a new subsystem. Gate: record cache hit/miss and prep cost, compare cold vs repeat, then redefine a function or change an input type and verify invalidation.

The explanation output must describe the actual chosen plan, not a separately maintained claim -- otherwise it becomes another lying surface.

column1: File-level `import` is a flat include, not a module
column2: Qu-Aspire lane; Ahmed 2026-09-11: "is a file acting as a class, can we make it a module instead"
column3: OPEN -- premise VERIFIED. `import "mymod.qu"` copies EVERYTHING from the file into the caller scope, functions and top-level variables alike, with no qualified form. Probe: mymod.qu holding SECRET=123 and function helper(a); main.qu doing import "mymod.qu" then print(helper(5)) => 10 and print(SECRET) => 123. The namespaced spelling does not exist: print(mymod.helper(5)) => "`mymod` is not defined". So a .qu file behaves as a flat include whose private state leaks, which is what makes it feel like a class rather than a module. Two open sub-questions for whoever takes this: (1) native modules DECLARE namespacing -- MODULE_EXPORTS lists ("xlsx", read/sheets/write) and ("codec", ...) -- so the mechanism exists in the engine, but I could not reach it: import "xlsx" looks for a FILE and fails, and bare xlsx.read says "`xlsx` is not defined". Either there is a third spelling I did not find or the namespaced native path is unreachable; establish which BEFORE designing on top of it. (2) Scoping inside functions is already correct and does not need changing: assignment is local (x=1 outside, x=99 inside, prints 1), reads fall through (prints 8), and `global` writes through (prints 42).
